title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 4–6). Grothendieck wants a combinatorial, purely algebraic model for the fundamental groupoids of the 'basic' pieces of the Teichmüller tower. In the genus-0 piece S_0T_{0,I}, I is the set of marked points or holes. The topological model on p.4 is a torsor P under a connected abelian Lie group U, here the circle and its powers, with universal cover Ũ and π = π_1(U), a free Z-module of finite type. The fundamental groupoid of P has Π(x,y) = Ũ_{y−x}, and composition is addition in Ũ.

General construction. Abstracting, take any extension of abelian groups (8) 0→π→E→Γ→0 and a Γ-torsor ε. One gets a connected π-groupoid E(ε) as follows.
- Objects are the points of ε.
- Hom(x,y) = E_{y−x}, the fibre of E over y−x ∈ Γ.
- Composition is addition in E.

On this page he gives the equivalent 'arrow-set' description, an action groupoid. Writing Σ for E and γ for Γ:
- Fl = Σ × ε.
- Source is pr_2.
- Target is (u,x) ↦ ū·x, the action of Σ on ε through Σ→γ.
- Composition is (u, vx)∘(v, x) = (uv, x).
All automorphism groups are canonically π, so this is a connected groupoid 'banded' by π.

Functoriality. Let γ'→γ be a group homomorphism and ε'→ε a compatible torsor morphism. The groupoid induced (pulled back) on ε' from Σ(ε) is canonically isomorphic to Σ'(ε'), where (11) 0→π→Σ'→γ'→0 is the pull-back extension Σ×_γ γ'. This is immediate from Hom(x',y') = Σ_{y−x} = Σ'_{y'−x'}.

Application. Using the earlier description (3) of S_0T_{0,I}, he states (12) S_0T_{0,I} ≃ Σ_I(ω(I)) as Z^I-groupoids. Here:
- ω(I) is a {±1}-torsor, presumably the two orientations / complex structures of the basic genus-0 piece.
- Σ_I (13) 0→Z^I→Σ_I→{±1}→0 is the pull-back of the universal-cover extension (S_I) 0→Z^I→R^I→U^I→0 along μ_2={±1}→U^I (map (4)).

The next page computes Σ_I by factoring through the diagonal μ_2→μ_2^I→U^I. The pull-back of 0→Z→R→U→0 along μ_2⊂U is 0→Z→(×2)Z→Z/2→0. So Σ_I is the push-out/pull-back of the diagonal of this standard extension. Concretely, the lift of −1 is (½,…,½), whose square is the diagonal element (1,…,1) of Z^I.

Topologically: the orientation-reversing / 'conjugation' generator squares to the product of all the elementary twists (the generators of the Z^I factor) at the I points. This is the familiar half-twist phenomenon, here encoded as an extension class in Ext(Z/2, Z^I).
errors: No mathematical error on this page.
The composition formula is written multiplicatively for an abelian group and has a crossed-out letter; the intended formula (u, v·x)∘(v, x) = (uv, x) is consistent with source = pr_2.
Notation drifts between E/Σ and Γ/γ across pages; this is harmless.

ideas.what: Connected π-groupoid attached to an abelian extension 0→π→E→Γ→0 and a Γ-torsor: Hom(x,y)=E_{y−x}, equivalently the action groupoid of E acting on the torsor through E→Γ
ideas.modern_name: Action (translation) groupoid E⋉ε; groupoid banded by π; fundamental groupoid of a torsor under a torus modelled by the universal-cover extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Ehresmann/Brown groupoid theory; band/gerbe language from Giraud)
ideas.where_published: Analogous ideas in SGA1/SGA7 (tame fundamental groups, tangential base points); this specific formulation is not known to be published

ideas.what: Pull-back of the torsor groupoid along γ'→γ equals the groupoid of the pulled-back extension
ideas.modern_name: Base change of extensions / functoriality of action groupoids

ideas.what: Description of the genus-0 basic Teichmüller groupoid S_0T_{0,I} as Σ_I(ω(I)), with Σ_I the extension of {±1} by Z^I pulled back from 0→Z^I→R^I→U^I→0 via −1 diagonal; the generator of {±1} squares to the product of all elementary twists
ideas.modern_name: Extended mapping class groupoid of genus-0 pieces with orientation reversal (tangential base points on the circle of directions; half-twist relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Teichmüller-tower / Lego literature: Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov; real/dihedral structures studied by Nakamura and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §3 discusses the Teichmüller tower, its genus-0 pieces and the {±1} (orientation) aspects only qualitatively

missed.claim: An explicit extension-theoretic encoding of the orientation-reversal (complex-conjugation) symmetry in the basic genus-0 Teichmüller groupoids: Σ_I is the diagonal pull-back of 0→Z→(×2)Z→Z/2→0. This is a small, clean unpublished detail of Grothendieck's own Lego construction including the {±1} action. It is consistent with later treatments rather than new to them.
missed.quote: S_0T_{0,I} ≃ Σ_I(ω(I)) ... où Σ_I est l'extension 0→Z^I→Σ_I→{±1}→0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck built orientation reversal (relevant to Gal(C/R) inside the GT/Teichmüller picture) into the base groupoids from the start. It may be of historical interest for the real/dihedral variants of GT.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a routine groupoid/extension construction. The genus-0 identification with the {±1}-extension is a nice explicit detail of the Teichmüller Lego, but matches later known structure (half-twist relations) and is not a surprising result.
transcription_corrections: Composition formula: read '(u, vx)∘(v,x) = (uv,x)'; the 'w' is a struck-through first attempt.
'Σ' and 'γ' in the transcription correspond to E and Γ of the previous page (Grothendieck's handwriting of E/Γ).
In (12), the stray 'ℓ' after S_0T_{0,I} is likely an artefact or part of '≃'; the marginal words above 'des Z^I-groupoïdes' read approximately 'comme ... des', and are uncertain.
